doc-knock-08.mechanism: These are the engine operating-point RAM variables (rpm_current, engine_load_current, iat_current) that nearly every closed-loop and map-lookup routine reads as the axis inputs to 2D/1D table lookups. rpm_current and engine_load_current are the near-universal (RPM, load) axis pair fed as fr4/fr5 into table_lookup_2D (0xBE8E4); iat_current is the axis input for intake-air-temperature compensation lookups. The sample functions compute: a knock/timing-advance correction loop (0x04378C) using a gbr-indexed per-cylinder workspace at 0xFFFF80FC with lag filters, deadband and clamps; IAT timing compensation (0x040420) multiplying a 2D 'IAT Activation' fraction by a 1D 'Timing Compensation A (IAT)' value; calculated-engine-torque interpolation across four torque maps (0x014EF4); boost-disable-during-fuel-cut thresholds (0x0141D6); a second IAT/IAM timing compensation path (0x042F48) using min/max/clamp helpers; target-boost base plus ECT and IAT compensations (0x0139F2); and a boost/load control loop with selectable maps and lag filters (0x03684A). 0xFFFF8258 is a float read in two of these routines (0x042F48, 0x03684A) used as a subtrahend in a correction/offset term.

mem-project_map_switch_patch_idea.mechanism: Two distinct groups appear. (1) The rev-limit / fuel-cut mechanism in 0x03B66C and 0x0BB404: RPM (rpm_current at 0xFFFF6624) is compared via fcmp against a set of calibration thresholds (Rev Limit On/Off tables at 0x000CC504..0x000CC518). 0x0F1000 is the target of a jmp @r0 (indirect branch) used immediately after loading one of two rev-limit tables, i.e. it is a code trampoline/dispatch address, not a scalar. 0x0F8900 is loaded as fr5 (=float32 8000.0) and passed into float_max against the fr15 value, i.e. a floating-point clamp/minimum-RPM constant for the rev-limit-on path. The outputs are the rev-limit state bytes at 0xFFFF7CB8 and the gbr-relative fuel-cut flags. (2) A data-copy/reporting mechanism in 0x05CF5E and 0x0BF4E0: 0x0FFAF8 is read byte-by-byte and copied into RAM scratch buffers (0xFFFFBF90-region and 0xFFFF5D27-region), alongside bytes from 0x00000FF8/0x00000FFC; this looks like assembling an ID/version descriptor block. 0x0FFC50 is loaded into VBR (the vector base register) during low-level init in 0x00F994's exception/reset path, and 0x00040001 is loaded into FPSCR. 0x09A3C2 and 0x040001 are inside instruction listings and act as code, not data (0x040001 is the FPSCR init value).

doc-rev-limit-patch-01.mechanism: This is the rev-limiter fuel-cut decision at 0x03B66C. It reads rpm_current (0xFFFF6624) into fr15, 0xFFFF65FC into fr14 and 0xFFFF620C into fr12. It passes fr14 to float_deadband_check(x, 0.0, 1.0). A non-zero result takes the 0x03B6AE path, which pairs with Rev Limit On/Off. A zero result takes the 0x03B6B8 path, which pairs with Rev Limit On(2)/Off(2). At 0x03B6C0 a hysteresis comparator runs against the selected pair. If rpm >= the On threshold (fr8), byte 0xFFFF7CB8+1 is set to 1. If rpm < the Off threshold (fr6), that byte is cleared. A second comparator does the same with Rev Limit On(3)/Off(3) into byte 0xFFFF7CB8+2. The +2 state is selected when all of these hold: 0x22CF4 returned 0; 0xFFFF65C0==1 or 0x299AC returned 2; 0xFFFF5E95==5 or 7, or 0x299BC returned 2. Otherwise the +1 state is used. The output is byte 0xFFFF7CB8+0, the cut-active flag. It is set when the selected state is 1. It is cleared only when the state is 0 and 0xFFFF620C < 'Rev Limit Fuel Resume (Boost)' (0x0CC518), so fuel stays cut until pressure falls. In 0x03B74A, when 0x22F92 returns 1 all three bytes are zeroed. The stub at 0x03B76E returns (byte0==1). The ROM looks patched. Both threshold-loading branches now do 'mov.l lit,r0 ; jmp @r0' to 0x000F1000, with a table address loaded into r2 in the delay slot. The literal slots 0x03B79C and 0x03B7A8 hold 0x000F1000 where table pointers would be expected, so the On threshold (fr8) is set by external code at 0x0F1000. 0x016102 builds a related flag 0xFFFF5D85. It is 1 when two status calls return 0, rpm < Rev Limit Off and 0xFFFF6155==0.

doc-transient-fuel-05.mechanism: Speed-limiter fuel-cut state machine with hysteresis and staged cut flags. Inputs: fr12 from RAM 0xFFFF65FC (compared against the speed-limit enable/disable tables, so presumably vehicle speed), rpm_current 0xFFFF6624, fr13 from 0xFFFF620C, and status bytes returned by 0x1CF16 (sp+4), 0x22CF4 (sp+8), 0x297A0 (sp+12) and 0x299BC (sp+16). If the 0x22CF4 result is 1, the thresholds are enable=0x0CC520 and disable=0x0CC528 (505). Otherwise they are enable=0x0CC51C (510) and disable=0x0CC524. The state byte 0xFFFF7CE0 holds 1 while the cut is active. Inactive: counter @7CE6 is incremented with saturation (uint8_add_sat) and @7CE7 is cleared. Entry happens if (speed >= enable, or sp+12==2, or sp+16==2) and rpm >= 0x0CC530 and sp+4==0. On entry the state is set to 1. If counter6 <= 0x0CBC0C, flags 7CE1..7CE5 are set to 1 and counter7 is preloaded with the 0x0CBC0B value. Counter6 is then zeroed. Not entering: if counter6 > 0x0CBC0C, flags 1..5 are cleared. Otherwise flags 3 and 4 are cleared and flag 5 stays 1. Active: counter @7CE7 is incremented with saturation and @7CE6 is cleared. Exit happens if any of these hold: (speed < disable and sp+12==0 and 1260 > fr13 and sp+16==0); (rpm < 0x0CC530 and 1260 > fr13); sp+4==1. On exit the state is set to 0. If counter7 <= 0x0CBC0B, flags 1..5 are cleared and counter6 is preloaded with the 0x0CBC0C value. Counter7 is then zeroed. Staying active: flags 1, 2 and 5 are set to 1. Once counter7 > 0x0CBC0B, flags 3 and 4 are also set, so the cut is staged and widens after the delay count. Outputs: state byte 0xFFFF7CE0 and cut flags 0xFFFF7CE1..7CE5. The function then tail-jumps to 0x3D2FC.

Value most likely 3, inferred from the listed uint8 and assuming the tool aligned the uint16 view to 0x0CBC0A.

When not entering, all flags are cleared only after counter6 > this; until then flag 5 is held. Copied into counter6 on exit. Value 3 (uint16 at this address is 0x033F).

mem-project_scheduler_event_queue.mechanism: This is a diagnostic/DTC (trouble-code) record manager working on a small array of fault records plus a dispatcher of per-module update routines gated by a single enable flag. 0xFFFF2064 is the base of an array of 5 fault records, each 12 bytes (stride confirmed by repeated 'add #12' loop steps in 0x010B3C, 0x010718, 0x010774; count 5 from 'mov #5,r10' / 'cmp/ge #5'). Each record holds a 4-byte field at offset +4 and a 1-byte counter/status at offset +8 (saturated at 0xFF: 'mov.w #0x00FF; cmp/ge; add #1' at 0x010B78-0x010B84). 0xFFFF2060 and 0xFFFF20A0 are scalar RAM operands/handles passed to the helper routines at 0xBDAAC, 0xBDB6E and 0xBDB80 (the lookup/accessor helpers). 0xFFFF20A4/0xFFFF20A8 are small status/result bytes written at the end (e.g. 'mov.l r2,@0xFFFF20A4', 'mov.b r2,@0xFFFF20A8'). Function 0x010B3C searches/compares the array (comparing a packed value via 0xBDAAC against a caller word, bumping the matching record's counter, and if no match and count<5 it appends a new record via 0xBDB80 writing the +4 field and +8=1). Function 0x010774 initialises/clears the 5 records. Function 0x010718 scans the array returning a flag. Function 0x010800 wraps 0x010B2A in critical_section_enter/exit (mask 0x00E0) for atomic record insertion. doc-architecture-03.mechanism: These are the two central engine-state scalars used across the ROM as gating/lookup inputs: rpm_current (0xFFFF6624, float32 RPM) and ect_current (0xFFFF6350, float32 engine coolant temp). Nearly every function in the pack loads them as float32 and compares them against calibration float constants (from the 0x000Cxxxx literal pool) to set boolean state flags, implement enable/disable thresholds and hysteresis, and feed table lookups. 0xFFFF65FC is a third float scalar used alongside them as a comparison input (compared to RPM at 0x015930 and to a constant at 0x026458). Concretely: (1) 0x022EB4 runs a counter at 0xFFFF65FA: if it reaches 63 it clears a byte flag at 0xFFFF65F7; otherwise, gated by a byte flag at 0xFFFF4166==1, an ect threshold (const 0xFFFF6350 vs float at mova pool) and a flag at 0xFFFF65AE==1, it sets the flag; then compares RPM to a float constant and either saturating-increments the counter via uint16_add_sat or zeroes it. (2) 0x012232 compares ect to constants 0x000C0248/0x000C024C to set/clear a byte flag at gbr+33 (hysteresis), and compares RPM to 0x000C0250/0x000C0254 to set/clear flag at 0xFFFF5BE6. (3) 0x022D2E gates on RPM>const, flag 0xFFFF65AE, and ect, running a LowPW_TableProcessor on descriptor 0x000AADE0 and managing a down-counter at 0xFFFF65E8. (4) 0x026410 combines several float thresholds on ect, 0xFFFF65FC and a stored float near 0xFFFF69D4 to write status bytes. (5) 0x015928 is a multi-state (state var at gbr+17) machine gating on 0xFFFF65FC, RPM, and thresholds from 0x000C14xx. (6) 0x01628E and 0x0152A8 run float_clamp_with_step on ect/RPM-derived values against table-pair constants to produce boolean indices. (7) 0x0139F2 computes a boost target: table_lookup_2D on "Target Boost_" indexed partly by RPM, times compensation table_lookup_1D on ect ("Target Boost Compensation (ECT)") and iat, multiplying the factors.

doc-turbo-character-03.mechanism: These two float32 calibration constants form an RPM rev-limiter hysteresis pair. rpm_current (0xFFFF6624) is compared against them to set/clear limiter flags. In FUNCTION 0x016102, after two helper calls gate the path, 'Rev Limit Off' (0xCC504 = 6680) is loaded into fr9 and compared fcmp/gt fr8(rpm) with fr9; if rpm is below 6680 (and additional byte flags at 0xFFFF6155 are clear) it computes a result (1/0) stored as a byte at 0xFFFF5D85. In FUNCTION 0x03B66C, a larger limiter state machine selects between 'Rev Limit On (2)' (0xCC508) and 'Rev Limit Off' (0xCC504) based on a byte flag at 0xFFFF65C0, loads it into fr6, and compares fcmp/gt fr15(rpm) with the On threshold (sets flag byte=1 at 0xFFFF7CB8+1 when rpm exceeds On) and with the Off threshold (clears flag=0 when rpm falls below Off). It then independently applies 'Rev Limit On (3)'/'Off (3)' (0xCC510/0xCC514) to byte+2, and a boost-based fuel-resume threshold (0xCC518) to the base flag byte. FUNCTION 0x0F1000 computes an effective On threshold: it adds an offset (fr8, selected from one of several small constants depending on a direction/comparison of fr9 vs fr6 and a flag at 0xFFFF65D0) to rpm in fr15, loads 'Rev Limit On' (0xCC500 = 6700) into fr8, then jumps back into 0x03B6B2 (the Off-branch continuation of the 03B66C function). So 0xCC500 'Rev Limit On' is the upper (engage) threshold and 0xCC504 'Rev Limit Off' is the lower (disengage) threshold of the same hysteresis band.

doc-transient-fuel-04.mechanism:
Two separate pieces of logic are bundled here.

(1) Transient (tau) fuelling term, FUNCTION 0x030C46. This is a three-term model, each term built as a temperature factor times a second factor.
- Inputs: ECT 0xFFFF6350 and an rpm copy at 0xFFFF7414.
- Two signed delta-style values at 0xFFFF73EC (r8-40) and 0xFFFF73D8 (r8-60). Their sign picks rising-load or falling-load tables.
- A mode byte from sub 0x21016, held at r15+8.
- A selector byte at 0xFFFF844F.

First branch, on the value at r8-40:
- If it is >= 0 (rising), with mode==2 and 0xFFFF844F==1, it uses 'Tau Input A Rising Load Activation' (desc 0xACB40) vs ECT. With mode==2 and the flag !=1 it uses desc 0xACB54. With mode !=2 it uses 0xACB68.
- If it is < 0 (falling), mode==2 uses 'Falling Load Activation' (0xACB7C). Otherwise it uses 'Falling Load Activation A' (0xACB90).
- The result goes to 0xFFFF73B8 (r8-92). An rpm-indexed factor (0xACBA4 or 0xACBB8) goes to r8-80.

Second branch, on the value at r8-60 being < 0:
- mode==2 uses 'Falling ... B' (0xACBCC). Otherwise it uses 'Falling ... C' (0xACBE0). Both are vs ECT, stored at r8-88.
- Further ECT/rpm factors go to r8-84, r8-76 and r8-72.
- In the >= 0 case, 2D tables (ECT x r8-100) are used instead.

Output is written to 0xFFFF73B4 (r8-96):
- out = ([r8-32]*[r8-76]*[r8-88] + [r8-36]*[r8-80]*[r8-92] + [r8-28]*[r8-72]*[r8-84]) * [r8-20].
- It is floored at 0 by float_max while counter 0xFFFF67EC < cal 0xCBC26.
- It is forced to 0 if counter 0xFFFF67EC < threshold (0xCBC2C or 0xCBC2A, chosen by flag gbr+150), or if sub 0x1CF5E returned 1.

(2) Filter plus accumulator, FUNCTIONS 0x03735A and 0x03740C/E.
- 0x03735A runs float_lag_filter with fr4=@0xFFFF7A60, fr5=@0xFFFF7A54, fr6=@0xFFFF7A58 and fr7 = the literal at 0x0373E8. It writes the result to 0xFFFF7A54.
- 0x03740E adds 0xFFFF7A54 to the float at 0xFFFF3194 every call, then writes it back via helper 0xBDBCC.
- On a rising edge of flag byte 0xFFFFAF3B (previous copy kept in 0xFFFF7A74), the sum is reset to 0, but only if 0xFFFF8EAC >= 720.0 (cal 0x0CC2B0).
- 0xFFFFAF3B is a widely used status flag. Other routines edge-detect it to count events (0xFFFF2F20 incremented with saturation), latch values (0xFFFF4144 -> 0xFFFF30C0), and set a one-shot edge flag (0xFFFF8EF3).

addresses.role: Entry of a small routine. It low-pass filters 0xFFFF7A60 via float_lag_filter (with 0xFFFF7A58 and the constant at 0x0373E8) and stores the result in 0xFFFF7A54.

Real start of the accumulator routine (push r14; the heuristic listing starts at 0x03740E). The matching pop of r14 is at 0x03744E.

Rising-load tau activation factor vs ECT, about 2.9-3.4 cold down to 0.5 hot. Selected when the delta at 0xFFFF73EC is >= 0, mode==2 and 0xFFFF844F==1. Stored to 0xFFFF73B8 and multiplied with an rpm factor into the tau output.
Falling-load tau activation factor vs ECT (1.42 down to 0.30). Selected when the delta is < 0 and mode==2. Stored to 0xFFFF73B8.
Falling-load tau activation factor vs ECT, used when mode !=2. Stored to 0xFFFF73B8. Flat 0.5 at every temperature.
Falling-load factor B vs ECT, used in the second term when the value at 0xFFFF73D8 is < 0 and mode==2. Stored to r8-88 and multiplied by [r8-32] and [r8-76].
Falling-load factor C vs ECT, used in the same term when mode !=2. Stored to r8-88.

Global status flag byte with value 1 = active. Many routines detect its rising edge (0->1) to reset the accumulator 0xFFFF3194, increment event counter 0xFFFF2F20, latch 0xFFFF4144 into 0xFFFF30C0, and set edge flag 0xFFFF8EF3. Its physical meaning (e.g. engine-running or key-on) is not shown.
Threshold of 720.0. The accumulator 0xFFFF3194 is reset on the AF3B rising edge only if 0xFFFF8EAC >= 720.
Float compared against 720.0 to permit the accumulator reset. Possibly a time or elapsed counter; units unknown.

doc-transient-fuel-04.inert_or_gated:
- 'Tau Input A Falling Load Activation A' is a constant 0.5 at every ECT, so its temperature dependence is inert.
- 'Falling Load Activation C' is 0 at 90-110 C, which zeroes that product term when hot and mode !=2.
- The tau output is forced to 0 while counter 0xFFFF67EC < cal 0xCBC2C/0xCBC2A, or when sub 0x1CF5E returns 1.
- The output is floored at 0 while counter 0xFFFF67EC < 0xCBC26.
- The accumulator reset is gated by AF3B edge AND 0xFFFF8EAC >= 720.0.
- The values at 0xCBC26, 0xCBC2A and 0xCBC2C are not shown.
evidence: 0x030D22-0x030D2A: sign of [0xFFFF73EC] chooses the 0xACB40/54/68 path (>=0) or the 0xACB7C/90 path (<0). Mode==2 and 0xFFFF844F==1 pick 0xACB40.
0x030D4E-0x030D5C: mode==2 gives 0xACB7C, otherwise 0xACB90. The result goes to r8-92.
0x030E58-0x030E72: mode==2 gives 0xACBCC (B), otherwise 0xACBE0 (C). The result goes to r8-88.
0x030E92-0x030EE0: three product terms summed with fmac, scaled by [r8-20], optionally passed through float_max(x,0), stored to 0xFFFF73B4.
0x03735A-0x037378: float_lag_filter(fr4=@7A60, fr5=@7A54, fr6=@7A58, fr7=const@0x0373E8) writes to 0xFFFF7A54.
0x037410-0x037448: if AF3B==1, prev 0xFFFF7A74==0 and 0xFFFF8EAC>=720, fr4=0. Otherwise fr4 = @3194 + @7A54. Then BDBCC(0xFFFF3194, fr4) and prev = AF3B.
0x087862-0x087882: on the AF3B rising edge (with 0xFFFFA5B0==1), 0xFFFF2F20 is incremented with uint16_add_sat.
0x05CAFE-0x05CB1A: 0xFFFF8EF3 = 1 on the AF3B rising edge, and 0xFFFF8EF2 = AF3B.

doc-boost-control-02.mechanism:
Open-loop boost target and wastegate-duty (WGDC) calculation, a boost-limit fuel-cut monitor, and wastegate solenoid PWM timer setup.

(1) Target boost, fn 0x0139F2. A 2D lookup of Target Boost uses fr4 = RAM 0xFFFF8558 (the 0–360 axis) and fr5 = rpm_current. The result goes to 0xFFFF5CE8. ECT comp (ect_current) goes to 0xFFFF5CEC and IAT comp (iat_current) to 0xFFFF5CF8. The final target is base × [0xFFFF5CF0] × ECT × [0xFFFF5CF4] × IAT, stored at 0xFFFF5CA8.
- 0xFFFF5CF0 is the Atm. Pressure comp. Fn 0x013B00 writes it from a 2D lookup of (0xFFFF6898, rpm).
- 0xFFFF5CF4 is the 1st-gear factor, written by fn 0x013B1A.
- If byte 0xFFFF5D03 == 90 (0x5A), the whole chain is bypassed and constant 0x0C0C04 is used as the target.
- The code then stores target − 0xFFFF6898 at 0xFFFF5CA4.
- Fragment 0x013B88 stores target − 0xFFFF620C at 0xFFFF5CA0, i.e. the boost error.

(2) 1st-gear comp, fn 0x013B1A. 0xFFFF5CFC is a ramped factor.
- If byte 0xFFFF6810 == 1 and speed 0xFFFF65FC <= 0x0C0C08 (1st Gear Speed Disable), the factor = max(prev − step[0x0C0C10], 1stGearComp[0x0C0C0C]).
- Otherwise the factor = min(prev + step, 1.0).
- 0xFFFF5CF4 = 1.0 if fn 0x1CF16 returns 1, else it copies 0xFFFF5CFC.

(3) WGDC, fn 0x013D66. RAM base is 0xFFFF5D14. Lookups:
- Initial WGDC (0xFFFF8558, rpm) → 0xFFFF5CB8.
- Max WGDC → 0xFFFF5CC8.
- WG Atm comp (0xFFFF6898, rpm) → 0xFFFF5CCC.
- WG IAT comp → 0xFFFF5CD0.
- Unnamed IAT table 0xAA89C → 0xFFFF5CD4.
- WG ECT comp → 0xFFFF5CD8.
- An rpm 1D table chosen by flags (0xAA950 / 0xAA968 / 0xAA95C) → 0xFFFF5CE4.

Effective max = Max × Atm × IAT × ECT, clamped to [0, 80.0] (literal 0x42A00000), stored at 0xFFFF5CC4.

Normal path: duty = clamp([0xFFFF5CAC] + Init × Atm × IAT × ECT + [0xFFFF5CB0], 0, effMax) → 0xFFFF5CBC, copied to 0xFFFF5CB4. 0xFFFF5CAC and 0xFFFF5CB0 are additive terms written elsewhere; most likely feedback terms.

An alternate path is enabled by cal byte 0x0C0BAC != 0 and gbr flags. It builds 0xFFFF5CC0 = min(tbl[0xFFFF5CE4] × Atm × tbl0xAA89C × ECT, duty), with an optional +0x0C0BC4 offset. It may copy that to 0xFFFF5CB4 and toggles flag 0xFFFF5D09.

Many inhibit conditions force 0xFFFF5CB4, 0xFFFF5CAC and 0xFFFF5CB0 to 0 and clear 0xFFFF5D09. These conditions are byte 0xFFFF85D7 == 1, gbr bytes 0xFFFF5D07 / 0xFFFF5D08 == 1, and helper return codes from 0x22F92, 0x2997C, 0x2998C, 0x297D0, 0x29A00 and 0x298B4.

The tail ramps toward the output: it builds a moving limit 0xFFFF5CC0 using step/floor constants 0x0C0BBC, 0x0C0BB8 and 0x0C0BC0, and outputs min(duty, limit) to 0xFFFF5C98. A deadband check (constant at 0x014250) clears ramp flag 0xFFFF5D04.

(4) Boost-limit fuel cut, fn 0x03BD3A.
- Limit = 2D lookup (0xFFFF6898, rpm) → 0xFFFF7CEC.
- float_clamp_with_step compares MAP 0xFFFF620C against the limit, with hysteresis from 0x0CC534. The state is held in 0xFFFF7CF0.
- If over the limit and 0x297D0() == 0, counter 0xFFFF7CE9 increments (saturating); otherwise it resets.
- When counter >= byte 0x0CBC0D, flag 0xFFFF7CE8 = 1 (fuel-cut request).

(5) WG PWM frequency, fns 0x005B14 / 0x005BF8.
- The uint16 at 0x0C009E (10000) is copied to RAM 0xFFFF4404.
- It is also multiplied (int32_fixmul) by [0xFFFF4138] and stored at 0xFFFF4408.
- Then timer registers are set up via short-literal addresses 0xFFFFF480/F482/F4E0/F4E2/F4EB (sign-extended).

addresses.role: Target Boost base table. 2D lookup with fr4 = 0xFFFF8558 (the 0–360 axis) and fr5 = rpm. Result (0xFFFF5CE8) is multiplied by atm, ECT, 1st-gear and IAT factors to give the boost target 0xFFFF5CA8.

Initial WGDC table (0xFFFF8558, rpm) → 0xFFFF5CB8. Its feedforward term Init × Atm × IAT × ECT is added to 0xFFFF5CAC + 0xFFFF5CB0 and clamped to [0, effective max] to give duty 0xFFFF5CBC / 0xFFFF5CB4.
Max WGDC table → 0xFFFF5CC8. Max × Atm × IAT × ECT, clamped to [0, 80.0], becomes the upper clamp 0xFFFF5CC4 for the duty.
Target boost ECT multiplier (input ect_current) → 0xFFFF5CEC, a factor in the target product.
Target boost IAT multiplier (input iat_current) → 0xFFFF5CF8, a factor in the target product.

Target boost atm-pressure multiplier, 2D (0xFFFF6898, rpm). Fn 0x013B00 writes it to 0xFFFF5CF0, which fn 0x0139F2 uses as a factor in the target product. The link is that offset -16 from 0xFFFF5D00 = 0xFFFF5CF0.

1st-gear target comp value (1.0). It is the floor of the downward ramp of 0xFFFF5CFC. The ramp is active when 0xFFFF6810 == 1 and speed <= 0x0C0C08; 0xFFFF6810 is assumed to be a 1st-gear flag. The result feeds factor 0xFFFF5CF4.

WGDC IAT multiplier → 0xFFFF5CD0. Applied to both the initial and max duty.
WGDC atm-pressure multiplier, 2D (0xFFFF6898, rpm) → 0xFFFF5CCC. Applied to initial, max and the alternate limit.

Boost limit for fuel cut, 2D (0xFFFF6898, rpm) → 0xFFFF7CEC. MAP 0xFFFF620C is compared against it with hysteresis 0x0CC534. A persistence counter (threshold byte 0x0CBC0D) then sets fuel-cut flag 0xFFFF7CE8.
WG solenoid PWM frequency/period constant (uint16 = 10000). Copied to RAM 0xFFFF4404 and scaled by [0xFFFF4138] into 0xFFFF4408 during timer setup. Physical units are not shown.
Atmospheric/barometric pressure (mmHg). Used as the 440–760 axis of all atm tables. It is subtracted from the target to give 0xFFFF5CA4 (gauge target).
Load/torque-request input on the 0–360 axis of Target Boost and both WGDC tables. Its exact quantity is not shown.
Manifold absolute pressure. Compared with the boost limit; target minus this value gives boost error 0xFFFF5CA0.

Computed WGDC (base + additive terms, clamped). Zeroed under inhibit conditions.
Rate-limited WGDC output: min(duty, ramp limit 0xFFFF5CC0).
Additive WGDC term, probably a feedback integral or learned correction; zeroed on inhibit.
Additive WGDC term, probably a feedback proportional correction; zeroed on inhibit.
Boost-limit fuel-cut flag. Its consumer is not shown.

doc-boost-control-02.inert_or_gated:
- ECT target comp (0x0C0CF4) is 1.0 everywhere, so it is inert.
- 1st-gear comp (0x0C0C0C) = 1.0. With step-up capped at 1.0 and step-down floored at 1.0, factor 0xFFFF5CFC sits at 1.0, so it is inert.
- IAT target comp is 1.0 at 0 °C and above; it only reduces target below 0 °C (0.849 at -20 °C, 0.950 at -10 °C).
- Target atm comp is 1.0 at 720 mmHg and above.
- WG ECT comp is 0 at ≤10 °C, which forces effective max = 0 and therefore duty = 0 (cold inhibit). It ramps to 1 by 20 °C.
- Effective max WGDC is clamped to 80.0%, so Max WGDC entries of 90 / 87.5 at 1600–2000 rpm, 360 axis are clipped at unity comps. The WG atm comp of 1.25 (4000 rpm, ≤670 mmHg) is also capped by this.
- Initial and Max WGDC rows at 6400 rpm are all 0 (duty → 0 at the top of the rpm axis). The 1600 rpm / 0-axis cells are also 0.
- Inhibit flags/helpers force WGDC and both additive terms to 0.
- Byte 0xFFFF5D03 == 90 replaces the target with constant 0x0C0C04 (value not shown).
- Cal byte 0x0C0BAC == 0 disables the alternate-limit logic (value not shown).
- Fuel cut needs count >= 0x0CBC0D (value not shown).
evidence: 0x013A1C-0x013A5A: Target Boost 2D (fr4 = [0xFFFF8558], fr5 = rpm) → 0xFFFF5CE8. ECT 1D → 0xFFFF5CEC, IAT 1D → 0xFFFF5CF8. Then fmul chain of offsets -24, -16, -20, -12, -8 from 0xFFFF5D00.

0x013A5C-0x013A66: target → 0xFFFF5CA8; target − [0xFFFF6898] → 0xFFFF5CA4.
0x013B0A-0x013B18: Atm comp 2D (fr4 = 0xFFFF6898, fr5 = rpm) stored to 0xFFFF5CF0.

0x013B38-0x013B62: 1st-gear ramp. When 0xFFFF6810 == 1 and speed <= 0x0C0C08: float_max(prev − [0x0C0C10], [0x0C0C0C]). Otherwise float_min(prev + step, 1.0). Result to 0xFFFF5CFC; copy or 1.0 to 0xFFFF5CF4.

0x014046-0x014074: [-104] + Init × Atm × IAT × ECT (fmac) + [-100], clamped [0, effMax] → 0xFFFF5CBC.
0x01400C-0x01403E: inhibit path zeros 0xFFFF5CB4, 0xFFFF5CAC and 0xFFFF5CB0.
0x01408C-0x0140AE: tbl[-48] × Atm × tbl0xAA89C × ECT, min with duty → 0xFFFF5CC0.

doc-boost-control-07.mechanism: Both addresses are single cells inside the two base wastegate-duty maps, not separate scalars. 0x0C0FE0 is 0x88 bytes (element 68) into "Max Wastegate Duty_" at 0x0C0F58. 0x0C11D8 is 0x88 bytes (element 68) into "Initial Wastegate Duty_" at 0x0C1150. Read as uint16 with a 1/256 scale, they give 20302/256 = 79.305 and 18037/256 = 70.457. Those are exactly the listed cells at RPM 3200 and the ninth breakpoint (240) of the 0–360 axis. The code never addresses the cells directly. Function 0x013D66 passes the descriptors 0xAA9B8 and 0xAA9D4 to table_lookup_2D (0xBE8E4). The inputs are fr5 = rpm_current (0xFFFF6624) and fr4 = RAM 0xFFFF8558, an unnamed load or boost-type variable on the 0–360 axis. Results: the Initial lookup is stored at 0xFFFF5CB8 (5D14-92) and the Max lookup at 0xFFFF5CC8 (5D14-76). Compensation tables are also looked up: Atm-pressure 2D from 0xFFFF6898 and rpm, stored at -72; IAT 1D at -68; unnamed IAT-indexed 0xAA89C at -64; ECT 1D at -60. Max-duty limit = Max × Atm × IAT × ECT, clamped by float_clamp_range to [0, 80.0] (literal 0x42A00000), stored at 0xFFFF5CC4 (-80). Initial duty = Initial × Atm × IAT × ECT + [5D14-104] + [5D14-100]. The fmac adds -104, then fadd adds -100; these are two additive terms, probably feedback or learning, and they are zeroed under some conditions. The sum is clamped to [0, max-limit at -80] and stored at -56 (0xFFFF5CDC). Depending on flags, -56 is copied to the duty variable at -96 (0xFFFF5CB4). Alternatively, a 1D rpm table chosen by state (0xAA950/0xAA968/0xAA95C) feeds a path at -52: × Atm × AA89C × ECT, then min against -56, optionally + 0xC0BC4 and min again. GBR flag byte 113 latches which path is active. Afterwards a step or rate stage (0xC0BBC, 0xC0BB8, 0xC0BC0, float_max/float_min) moves the target at -88 toward -96. The result is written to -124, which equals 0xFFFF5C98, the GBR base; it is probably the final commanded wastegate duty. A deadband check of -96 against -88 clears GBR flag 108.

addresses.role: Base of "Max Wastegate Duty_" map (descriptor 0xAA9B8). Looked up with rpm and 0xFFFF8558, multiplied by the Atm/IAT/ECT compensations, clamped to [0, 80] and used as the ceiling for the duty command at 0xFFFF5CC4.
One cell of the Max Wastegate Duty map: element 68, RPM 3200, axis value 240. uint16 20302 × 1/256 = 79.305 %. Reached only through table interpolation.

Base of "Initial Wastegate Duty_" map (descriptor 0xAA9D4). Looked up with rpm and 0xFFFF8558 and stored at 0xFFFF5CB8. It is the feed-forward base of the duty command: × comps + adders, clamped to [0, max].
One cell of the Initial Wastegate Duty map: element 68, RPM 3200, axis value 240. uint16 18037 × 1/256 = 70.457 %.

doc-boost-control-07.inert_or_gated: The max-duty product is clamped to 0..80.0 (literal 0x42A00000 at 0x014004). Max-map cells of 85–90 % can therefore only take effect if the compensations pull the product below 80; the 87.5/90 cells at 1600–2000 rpm, top of the axis, are capped at 80 when the compensations are 1. The RPM 6400 row and the RPM 1600/axis-0 cell are 0 in both maps, so duty there is 0. Initial duty is clamped to [0, max-limit]. Several status flags send execution to 0x01400C: r10 from 0xFFFF85D7 == 1, helper results ==1 or ==2, GBR bytes 111 or 112 == 1. That path zeroes 0xFFFF5CB4, 5CAC and 5CB0, forcing the duty to 0 and clearing the additive terms. If byte 0xC0BAC == 0, only the plain initial-duty path runs (flags 16/20); its value is not shown.
evidence: 013DF6 loads descriptor 0xAA9D4 (Initial WGDC) and calls table_lookup_2D with fr5 = rpm_current, fr4 = [0xFFFF8558]. The result is stored to 0xFFFF5D14-92.
013E3C loads descriptor 0xAA9B8 (Max WGDC) with the same inputs. The result is stored at 5D14-76.
013E84–013EA8: [-76]×[-72]×[-68]×[-60] goes to float_clamp_range(lo = 0, hi = 80.0) and is stored at -80.
0x0C0FE0 - 0x0C0F58 = 0x88 = element 68 = row RPM 3200, column 8 (240). 20302/256 = 79.305 matches the listed cell.
0x0C11D8 - 0x0C1150 = 0x88. 18037/256 = 70.457 matches the Initial map cell at RPM 3200, axis 240.
014182–01418C: min(-96, -88) is stored at 5D14-124 = 0xFFFF5C98, the GBR base.
doc-boost-control-07.not_shown: The identity of the 0–360 axis variable 0xFFFF8558 is not shown; it may be boost target, load or a similar quantity. The table_lookup_2D argument-to-axis mapping and the descriptor storage type and scale are not shown; the uint16/256 reading is inferred from the matching values. Not shown: what writes the adders at 5D14-104 and -100; the values of 0xC0BAC, 0xC0BB8, 0xC0BBC, 0xC0BC0 and 0xC0BC4; the meaning of the helper-function flags. Also not shown is where 0xFFFF5C98 and 0xFFFF5CB4 go downstream (the solenoid output driver).

doc-boost-control-01.mechanism: Two distinct mechanisms appear. (1) 0x0C009E is the 'Wastegate Duty Cycle Frequency' calibration word (uint16 = 10000). Two functions (0x005B14, 0x005BF8) read it with mov.w @r3 and program it into a hardware timer/PWM peripheral block at 0xFFFF4404 (a 16-bit timer control structure): the value is written to the timer period register, and in 0x005B14 it is also fed through int32_fixmul before being stored as a compare/duty value. These set up the wastegate solenoid PWM frequency. (2) 0x054852/0x054858 is a periodic boost/wastegate control routine (dispatched from the big init/scheduler table at 0x04AC6A alongside 0x0549FA at 0x04AC70). It sets GBR to 0xFFFF8B50 and uses GBR-relative byte/float accesses to a RAM state block based there. 0xFFFF8B50 itself holds a float that is read, updated (fsub against table_lookup_1D results and float_max clamps), and written back repeatedly — it is the running/filtered boost-error or integrator term for the controller. 0x0549FA is a companion routine applying a float_lag_filter (reads rpm_current, filters state in the 0xFFFF8BC4 block), and 0x054A5A zeroes that filter state block when a mode check returns 1 (reset path).

addresses.role: uint16 calibration constant (10000) = wastegate PWM frequency; loaded and written into timer period register at 0xFFFF4404 and, in 0x005B14, passed through int32_fixmul to form a compare value
GBR base and float working variable of the boost/wastegate controller; read, differenced against lookup/max results, and stored back each pass (controller integrator/error state)
entry of the boost/wastegate control routine (prologue saving r12-r14), falls into 0x054858 body; invoked from scheduler table at 0x04AC6A
companion lag-filter routine (filters rpm/boost state in 0xFFFF8BC4 block); invoked from scheduler table at 0x04AC70
reset routine: when mode helper at 0x22F92 returns 1, zeroes (fldi0) the filter/controller state block at 0xFFFF8BC4

doc-boost-control-01.inert_or_gated: In 0x054858 the whole table_lookup/fmac boost-correction path is gated: it is skipped (bra to 0x054990) when the enable byte at GBR+128 is zero (set from rpm thresholds 0xD6720/0xD6724), or taken to the fixed-value branches 0x054978/0x05495E when r13 or r14 (state bytes at 0xFFFF65C0/0xFFFF64F5) equal 1. The uint8_add_sat counter path at 0x0549A2 only runs when r13, r14 and GBR+128 are all set. 0x054A5A's zeroing block runs only when helper 0x22F92 returns exactly 1. No zero-multiplier or dead calibration constant proven inert in this cal.
evidence: 0x005C06/0x005B18/0x005B38 load 0x0C009E as mov.w and store into 0xFFFF4404 structure (period at @r4, compare at @(4,r4)), with critical_section_enter/exit wrapping — timer/PWM programming
0x005B20 passes the 0x0C009E value through int32_fixmul before storing as the 12(r15)->@(4,r4) compare value

0x054864/0x0548BC/0x054906/0x05492C/0x05495E/0x054978 all reference 0xFFFF8B50: it is set as GBR, and separately fmov.s read/written as a float that is subtracted from fr13/table values and clamped via float_max (0xBE960)

GBR+128 enable byte set/cleared from fcmp against RPM thresholds at 0xD6720/0xD6724 in 0x054858
doc-boost-control-01.not_shown: The scaling/units applied to 0x0C009E inside int32_fixmul and the actual peripheral meaning of 0xFFFF4404 fields (whether it is the wastegate GPT/PWM channel) are not confirmed by the pack. The full layout and physical meaning of the 0xFFFF8B50/0xFFFF8BC4/0xFFFF8BD0 RAM blocks, the contents of the 1D tables at 0xAEFE4/0xAEFF0/0xAEFFC, and the constants at 0xD670C-0xD6724 are not decoded. Whether this controller output ultimately drives the same PWM programmed from 0x0C009E is not shown.

mem-feedback_ect_axis_celsius.mechanism: This function computes a 'Tau Input A' fuel-film / wall-wetting activation factor. It reads ect_current (coolant temp, 0xFFFF6350) into fr15 and rpm_current (0xFFFF6624) as inputs, and determines a load-direction state (rising vs falling, encoded 1 or 2 in the byte at (8,r15) / [8]). Based on that state it selects one of several 1D activation tables indexed by coolant temperature and looks them up via table_lookup_1D (0xBE830) with fr4=ect_current. The two addresses of interest are the descriptors for the rising-load (0x000ACB40 -> table data at 0x0CD6E6) and falling-load (0x000ACB7C -> table data at 0x0CD746) activation curves, each a 16-point curve over coolant temperature -40..110C. The chosen curve result is stored to a scratch frame slot (offset -92 from r8) and later combined by a chain of fmul/fmac operations with other looked-up factors (2D tables keyed on temp and another input, plus further 1D curves) to produce a final activation multiplier, which is clamped with float_max (0xBE960) against 0.0 and written to scratch slot -96 from r8. Various gated bytes at gbr offsets (148,149,150) and a RPM threshold comparison (0xCBC26/0xCBC2A/0xCBC2C) decide whether the full calculation runs or the output is forced to 0.0.

addresses.role: Table data for 'Tau Input A Rising Load Activation': 16 float values over coolant-temp breakpoints -40..110C; selected (descriptor 0xACB40) when load is rising and the mode byte at 0xFFFF844F != 1, looked up with ect_current to give a rising-load activation factor stored at frame slot -92(r8).

Table data for 'Tau Input A Falling Load Activation': 16 floats over same coolant-temp axis; selected (descriptor 0xACB7C) when load is falling (state!=2) and mode byte at 0xFFFF844F != 1, looked up with ect_current to give a falling-load activation factor stored at slot -92(r8).
ect_current (coolant temp), loaded into fr15 and used as fr4 X-axis input to all these 1D/2D table lookups.
rpm_current, loaded into fr8 early; part of the engine-state inputs.
Descriptor pointer for the rising-load activation table, loaded into r4 then passed to table_lookup_1D.
Descriptor pointer for the falling-load activation table, loaded into r4 then passed to table_lookup_1D.
Descriptor for 'Tau Input A Falling Load Activation A', alternate falling-load table selected when state==2.
Descriptor for a rising-load activation table variant selected when mode byte at 0xFFFF844F == 1 and state==1.
16-bit RPM/count threshold compared (via (84,gbr)) against r11 (0xFFFF67EC) to gate whether the activation path runs; alternate value when activation flag at gbr+150 set.
Alternate 16-bit threshold used when gbr+150 activation flag is set.
16-bit threshold compared against r14 to decide whether final result is floored to 0.0 via float_max.

mem-feedback_ect_axis_celsius.inert_or_gated: Output is forced to 0.0 (fldi0 fr8 stored at -96(r8)) if the count in r11 (0xFFFF67EC) < threshold (0xCBC2A/0xCBC2C), or if byte @r15==1, so the whole table result can be gated off. The activation flag at gbr+150 is set to 1 unless r13 (0xFFFF6254) and r12 (0xFFFF65C0) are both nonzero AND fr14 > table[-60] AND fr0 < table[-40]; when flag set the alternate threshold path is taken. Exact calibration values of 0xCBC26/2A/2C bytes not shown, so cannot state which branch is live.

mem-feedback_ect_axis_celsius.not_shown: The absolute scaling/units of the stored activation factor, the actual runtime values of the gating bytes at 0xCBC26/2A/2C and the mode byte 0xFFFF844F in this calibration, how the final slot -96(r8) result feeds the fuel model downstream, and the contents/axes of the referenced 2D tables (0xAD82C, 0xAD810/0xAD7F4) and the other 1D correction curves. Whether rising vs falling branch is actually reached depends on load-direction computation not present in this listing.

mem-project_knock_flag_channel.mechanism:
Per-cylinder knock detection that drives the knock-flag consumers. Function 0x04378C sets GBR=0xFFFF80FC, so @(176,gbr)=0xFFFF81AC is the cylinder index, @(190,gbr)=0xFFFF81BA and @(191,gbr)=0xFFFF81BB.

Signal path: it reads raw input 0xFFFF4304 and clamps it to >=0. It passes that through 1D table 0xAE284, applies per-cylinder byte offsets, clamps to >=0 again and stores the result as the knock signal at 0xFFFF8138.

Statistics: it keeps per-cylinder lag-filtered statistics in float arrays off 0xFFFF8158 (+36 and +68 a mean-like level, +20 a deviation-like spread, +4 a limit looked up from rpm).

Thresholds: two rpm x load 2D tables, selected per cylinder through pointer arrays 0x063E58 and 0x063E68, give gains. Threshold 1 (0xFFFF8154) = level + gain44*dev, clamped to [0xD2D88, 0xD2D8C]. Threshold 2 (0xFFFF8158) = level + gain44*gain40*dev, clamped to [0xD2D88, 0xD2D90].

Flags: if signal >= threshold 1 and the word counter 0xFFFF67EC >= 250 (cal 0x0D29DC), 0xFFFF81BA (knock flag) is set to 1. 0xFFFF81BB (heavy-knock flag) is also set to 1 when signal >= threshold 2. Otherwise both are 0.

Consumers:
- Fine knock correction 0x0463BC reads 81BA. If 0 it takes the advance path (Fine Correction Advance Delay/Value). If 1 it retards: by 0xD2F64 when 81BB==1, else by 'Fine Correction Retard Value'. Both paths clamp to the Advance/Retard Limits.
- 0x042F48 (IAT timing compensation / IAM logic): when 81BA is set it decrements a value by 0xD2CE0.
- 0x044DE0 and 0x046856 count knock-free time: 16-bit counters 0xFFFF8224 and 0xFFFF8294 increment, saturating at 0xFFFF, while 81BA==0 and reset to 0 when it is set.
- 0x04629C gates a lag filter on 81BA==0.
- 0x043D70 reads 81BA and bumps a per-cylinder knock event count (pointer array 0x063E78) on a 0->1 edge; the previous state is kept at @(221,gbr).
- Init routine 0x043FEC clears 81BA and 81BB, sets the cylinder index to 0xFF and seeds the arrays.

addresses.role: Knock-detected flag (byte, GBR+190). Set 1 when the filtered knock signal >= threshold 1 and the enable counter >= 250, else 0. Read by fine knock correction (advance vs retard), IAT/IAM timing logic, knock-free counters, the knock event counter and a filter gate.
Instruction storing 1 to 0xFFFF81BA (delay slot of bra) on the path where the signal also exceeds threshold 2; 81BB is then also set to 1.
Instruction storing r0 to 0xFFFF81BA. Reached with r0=1 (signal between thresholds 1 and 2) or r0=0 (below threshold 1 or counter < 250).
GBR base of the knock-detection state block. Used for cylinder index (+176), flags (+190/+191), previous flag (+221) and per-cylinder byte arrays (+182, +186, +212, +216).
ldc r0,gbr loading 0xFFFF80FC as GBR in the knock detection routine.
uint16 calibration, value 250. Minimum value of the counter word 0xFFFF67EC before the knock flag may be set (enable/settling gate). What 0xFFFF67EC counts is not shown.

Heavy-knock flag (GBR+191). Set 1 only when the knock flag is set and the signal >= threshold 2, else 0. Fine correction uses it to pick the larger retard step 0xD2F64 instead of 'Fine Correction Retard Value'.
Code in function 0x044394, which is not shown; presumably another reference to the knock flag or state block.
mov.b @r5,r7: fine knock correction loads the knock flag 0xFFFF81BA.
tst r7,r7: branch on the knock flag. Zero takes the advance/delay path, nonzero jumps to the retard path at 0x046618.

mem-project_knock_flag_channel.inert_or_gated: Knock flag setting is gated by word counter 0xFFFF67EC >= 250 (0x0D29DC). Both flags are forced to 0 below threshold 1. Threshold 1 is clamped to [0xD2D88, 0xD2D8C] and threshold 2 to [0xD2D88, 0xD2D90]; those float values are not shown. Cal byte 0xD298B, when nonzero, disables the bad-state change handling that sets @(192,gbr). No zero multiplier found.
evidence: 0x043796/0x043798: GBR=0xFFFF80FC, so @(190,gbr)=0xFFFF81BA and @(191,gbr)=0xFFFF81BB.
0x043B34-0x043B62: compare signal @(-32,r9) vs threshold @(-4,r9), check counter r11 (from 0xFFFF67EC) >= *0xD29DC (250), compare vs @r9, then write 81BA/81BB.
0x043ABC-0x043B08: thresholds = level + table gain * deviation, with clamps at 0xD2D88/0xD2D8C/0xD2D90.
0x04384A-0x043874: per-cylinder 2D lookups vs rpm_current and engine_load_current through pointer arrays 0x063E58/0x063E68.

Contents of function 0x044394 (0x0443C4) and of the 8 other referencing functions. Whether 0xFFFF81BA is also written via indexed or other GBR access elsewhere.

doc-ssm-read-patch-00.mechanism: This is a diagnostic/communication service handler (looks like a bytestream request parser and response builder, consistent with a UDS/K-line or CAN diagnostic routine). The function at 0x09A3BA (prologue plus register save block starting ~0x09A3AC) takes a request code in r4, validates it against ranges (values 0..3 and a sub-decode loop subtracting 3), then parses a variable-length record. It reads a record descriptor from a RAM scratch buffer based at 0xFFFFB2F4 (a 16-bit count/length and a byte stream starting at +3), iterates that many entries, and for each entry reads a 3-byte big-endian token (sign-extended first byte as a type/opcode: -1, -12, -14 select copy lengths 0/3/1). For tokens below a limit of 0x0350 it dispatches through a function-pointer table at 0x0006423C (index = token<<2) to compute a response byte; for tokens >= 0x0350 it treats the high bits as a far pointer (OR with 0x000F0000) and byte-copies bytes into an output buffer at 0xFFFFB3F4. On error it calls an error/negative-response routine at 0x00098686 with the service code (-88 = 0xA8) and code 2; on success it builds a positive response via helpers 0x0009CFEE (append/format), 0x0009B770, and 0x0009CABE (send/finalize) using a stack frame. 0x09A3C2 is the instruction that extends the incoming request code (r4) to a word for range validation; 0x09A3B0 is part of the callee-saved-register push preamble; 0x09A3C2/0x09A3B0 themselves are not data addresses, they are code sites. The sibling function 0x09A2EA is a related service that reads a mode/state byte at 0xFFFFB018, checks it equals 2/3, sets a flag at 0xFFFFB01C, and emits either an error (code in r14: 18/19/34) or a positive response built the same way.

addresses.role: Instruction (extu.w r4,r5): zero-extends the incoming request/service argument to 16 bits for the subsequent range checks (>3, and the sub-3 decode loop). Entry/decode point of the service handler.
Instruction (mov.l r10,@-r15): part of the callee-saved register save sequence (r8-r14, pr) at the function's true prologue just before 0x09A3BA.
RAM scratch/request buffer base: 16-bit length/count at +0, token stream at +3; also used to stash a word count for the response. (referenced via 0x09A4DC literal)
Output/response byte buffer written by the copy and table-dispatch loop.
Function-pointer table (jump table) indexed by token<<2; each entry computes a response byte for tokens below 0x0350.
Mode/state byte read and compared to 2/3 in sibling handler 0x09A2EA.
Flag byte set to 1 when the state check passes in 0x09A2EA.

doc-ssm-read-patch-00.inert_or_gated: Token limit constant 0x0350 gates table-dispatch vs. far-pointer-copy path. Copy length is fixed by token type: -1->0 bytes, -12(0xF4)->3 bytes, -14(0xF2)->1 byte; any other first-byte value takes the dispatch/error branch (r4=0, no copy). Service code is the constant 0xA8 (-88) in this function and 0x85 (-123) in the sibling. No zero-multiplier arithmetic seen.
evidence: 0x09A3C2 extu.w r4,r5 then cmp/gt #3 and the subtract-3 loop establish request-code validation.
0x09A414 loads limit 0x0350; 0x09A45A cmp/hs r8,r1 branches on token vs 0x0350.
0x09A45E loads table base 0x0006423C; 0x09A464 mov.l @(r0,r5) with r0=token<<2 indexes it; 0x09A466 jsr @r6 calls the entry.
0x09A444-0x09A456 copy loop writes bytes to r10 (=0xFFFFB3F4) with length selected by token type bytes -1/-12/-14.
0x09A47A/0x09A482 call 0x00098686 with service 0xA8 and code 2 on error (negative response).
0x09A49E/0x09A4A8 call 0x0009CFEE and 0x09A4C2 call 0x0009CABE to assemble/send a positive response via a stack frame.
0x09A2F0-0x09A326 read 0xFFFFB018, compare to 3/2, set 0xFFFFB01C=1, select error codes 18/19/34.
doc-ssm-read-patch-00.not_shown: The pack does not reveal the transport layer (CAN vs K-line), the exact diagnostic protocol/service IDs these numeric codes map to, the contents and meaning of the jump table at 0x0006423C, the layout/source of the request buffer at 0xFFFFB2F4 (who fills it), or what the far-pointer copies (token>=0x0350 with high bits 0x0F0000) actually read. It also does not show units or calibration tables, so none of these are g/rev/km/h/Celsius physical quantities.

doc-architecture-02.mechanism: This is reprogramming/bootloader (CAN flash reflash) code. 0xFFFFBFA0 is a RAM pointer cell that holds the address of the currently-received message/packet buffer. At 0xA52 and 0xA98 a value (a pointer/handle returned from a sub at 0x12C) is stored into @0xFFFFBFA0; at 0xA9C and 0x0C0/0xE2 it is read back (mov.l @r1,r3 / mov.l @r2,r4) and used as the data pointer passed to the response/transmit helper at 0x04C2. At reset-vector-like entries (0x40, 0x4C) the literal 0xFFFFBFA0 is loaded into r15, i.e. it is used as the initial stack-pointer top (the download/execute stub sets SP there before jmp @r4). So 0xFFFFBFA0 is both the top of a scratch stack and the base of a RAM cell holding the active buffer pointer. 0xFFFFBFFC is a 32-bit flag/signature cell: at 0x688-0x6A2 it is read and compared against the constant 0x5AA5A55A; if it does NOT match, a recovery/erase path (bsr 0x7E0 with r4=7, then flash routines via helper 0xEE4) is taken. At 0x752-0x756 the constant 0x5AA5A55A is written into 0xFFFFBFFC, then control jumps to 0x40 (re-enter with SP=0xFFFFBFA0). So 0xFFFFBFFC is a persistent 'reprogramming-in-progress / valid' magic marker that gates whether the flash-update sequence runs and is re-armed before re-entry.

addresses.role: RAM pointer cell holding the active received-message/data buffer pointer; written at 0xA52/0xA98 with a handle from sub 0x12C, read at 0xA9C/0x0C0/0x0E2 as the data pointer for the transmit helper 0x04C2. Same literal also loaded into r15 at 0x40/0x4C as the initial stack-pointer top for the download/execute stub.
32-bit signature/flag cell compared to 0x5AA5A55A to decide whether the flash-reprogram sequence proceeds; written with 0x5AA5A55A at 0x756 to re-arm before jumping back to the entry at 0x40.
Adjacent RAM pointer cell written at 0xBA with r4 (received frame pointer + 2); companion to 0xFFFFBFA0 save area.
Byte RAM flag read at 0x4E4 selecting between two handlers (jsr 0x344 vs 0x5CC); set at 0x74E. Part of the same reprogram state block.

doc-architecture-02.inert_or_gated: The flash path at 0x6A8+ is gated on 0xFFFFBFFC == 0x5AA5A55A: if the cell already holds the magic the mismatch-recovery branch (0x694/0x6E2 with r4=7) is skipped; if not, the erase/recovery path runs. At 0xA58 a separate byte flag @0xFFFFBFBC is tested: if ==1 it is cleared to 0 (mov #0; mov.b r2,@r4), gating the pointer store. No zero-multiplier or always-false constant found; both branches are reachable depending on these RAM flags.
evidence: 0xA52: mov.l r0,@r3 with r3=0xFFFFBFA0 stores sub-0x12C result; 0xA9C/0xAB4 read @0xFFFFBFA0 as pointer, add offset, store back, pass to 0x04C2 transmit helper
0x40/0x4C: mov.l @(...),r15 = 0xFFFFBFA0 loads the literal into the stack pointer at an entry stub (jmp @r4 follows)
0x0C0: mov.l @r2,r4 with r2=0xFFFFBFA0 reads the saved buffer pointer; 0xBA stores r4 (frame+2) into 0xFFFFBFA4
0x68C-0x690: load 0xFFFFBFFC, mov.l @r2,r0, cmp/eq with literal 0x5AA5A55A at 0x72C; bt skips recovery
0x752-0x756: mov.l r3,@r2 writes 0x5AA5A55A into 0xFFFFBFFC, then jsr 0x0040 (re-entry) with r4=handler
0xA58: mov.b @0xFFFFBFBC, cmp/eq #1, conditional clear to 0 before pointer store
doc-architecture-02.not_shown: The pack does not show what sub 0x12C returns (the exact handle/value stored at 0xFFFFBFA0), nor the contents/layout of the message structures at those pointers. It does not show the flash erase/program helpers (0x7E0, 0xEE4, 0xAD8, 0x04C2) internals, the meaning of the 0x000FFFFC/0x0017FFFC flash-region constants in detail, or who else writes 0xFFFFBFFC/0xFFFFBFA0 via indexed or GBR access. Units/engine-calibration meaning do not apply — these are bootloader state cells, not a calibration table.

mem-feedback_dont_attribute_from_magnitu.mechanism:
The six addresses fall into three unrelated groups.

(1) Ratio correction in function 0x039530. It reads a fraction x from 0xFFFF7800 and checks 1-x against a deadband (0, const@0x039750). If 1-x is inside the band, the output 0xFFFF7BAC (=7BC0-20) is set to 0. Otherwise it computes r = 1/(1-x) - 1, i.e. x/(1-x), via float_safe_div. It looks up table 0xAD258 with ECT (ect_gated_c 0xFFFF6354) and stores the result in 0xFFFF7BC0. The byte flag 0xFFFF7448 then chooses the path:
- flag = 1: r is clamped to [0, *0xCC3EC] without the ECT factor.
- flag ≠ 1: r × ECT factor is clamped to [0, *0xCC3F0].
The result goes to 0xFFFF7BAC. When byte 0xFFFF782C is 0, the code calls 0x03961C with r4=0xFFFF7BAC instead. The function then compares 0xFFFF7BAC with 0xFFFF798C, or deadband-tests 0xFFFF798C, to decide whether to copy 0xFFFF7BAC into 0xFFFF7BA8 and 0xFFFF7BA4 or to zero 0xFFFF7BA8. 0xFFFF7BA8 is later packed into the snapshot block at GBR+42.

(2) Function 0x038E6E (GBR=0xFFFF7B7C). It is entered only when rpm_current < *0xCC3C4 and further flag conditions hold. It looks up 0xAD208 against rpm_current; that table's data is at 0xCE8B4. The result (stack+120) is passed as fr5 to subroutine 0x03949E, together with:
- fr4: a correction value from stack+4,
- r4: a byte counter at GBR+32 (0xFFFF7B9C),
- r5: a calibration byte at 0xCBBFF.
The output goes to 0xFFFF7B7C (7BA0-36). Sister tables 0xAD21C, 0xAD230 and 0xAD244 play the same role for the other three channels. The shape suggests a per-RPM rate or filter gain, but that is unconfirmed.

(3) Snapshot packer at 0x0243BA. At 0x0243C6/0x0243C8 it saves GBR and loads GBR = 0xFFFF683C. It then converts many float RAM signals into a packed block based at 0xFFFF683C using axis_frac_to_uint16 (GBR+0..48) and axis_frac_to_uint8 (GBR+50..82). The signals include ECT, IAT, load, MAF, rpm, 0xFFFF798C and 0xFFFF7BA8. At 0x0245A4 it loads the scale constant at 0x02471C (raw 0x3EB40000 = 0.3515625). With offset -20.0 (const@0x024718, raw 0xC1A00000) this quantizes 0xFFFF7E90 and 0xFFFF7E94 to bytes at GBR+60/61, and the same scale is reused for later bytes.

0x036D14 is the entry of a separate routine in the 0x036C4E listing. If flag 0xFFFF7C18 = 1, it decays float 0xFFFF7A18 by *0xCC254, floored at 0. Otherwise, when the uint16 counter 0xFFFF7A1C ≥ *0xCBC6A, it subtracts *0xCC250 per call, floored at 0 or at *0xCC24C depending on 0xFFFF67EC < *0xCBC6C and two status calls. The routine just before it (0x036C4E) increments 0xFFFF7A1C with saturation.

addresses.role: 1D table descriptor looked up with ect_gated_c (0xFFFF6354), X axis -40..110 C. Output stored to 0xFFFF7BC0 and used as a multiplier on x/(1-x) before clamp, only when flag 0xFFFF7448 != 1.

Data of the RPM-indexed table (descriptor 0xAD208, axis 800-3200 rpm), looked up with rpm_current in 0x038E6E. Value is passed as fr5 into subroutine 0x03949E, whose result is written to 0xFFFF7B7C. Possibly a filter or step gain (hunch for that interpretation).

Entry point of a decay routine: decrements float 0xFFFF7A18 by calibration step 0xCC254 or 0xCC250, floored at 0 or at 0xCC24C. Gated on flag 0xFFFF7C18, flag 0xFFFF726C, counter 0xFFFF7A1C >= 0xCBC6A and 0xFFFF67EC < 0xCBC6C.
ldc r0,gbr instruction that sets GBR = 0xFFFF683C at the start of the snapshot/packing function.
Loads scale 0.3515625 (float at 0x02471C) into fr14. Used with offset -20.0 to quantize 0xFFFF7E90 and 0xFFFF7E94 into uint8 at GBR+60/61, and reused for later bytes (62-64, 66).
Base of a RAM block of quantized (uint16/uint8) copies of engine signals written via GBR-relative stores by 0x0243BA. Who reads it is not shown; a diagnostic or logging snapshot is a guess.

mem-feedback_dont_attribute_from_magnitu.inert_or_gated:
- 0xAD258 (ECT factor): every value is 1.0, so the ECT multiplier in 0x039530 has no effect. The two flag paths differ only in clamp ceiling (*0xCC3EC vs *0xCC3F0, values not shown).
- 0xAD208/0xCE8B4: every value is 0.099976 (~0.1), so this gain has no RPM dependence.
- 0x039530 output: forced to 0 when 1-x falls in the deadband (const at 0x039750, value not decoded).
- 0x038E6E body: skipped (bsr 0x0392C4 instead) when rpm_current >= *0xCC3C4, when 0xFFFF90BD = 0, or when 0xFFFF7C68 = 1 with 0xFFFF7D2E = 0.
evidence: 0x039598-0x0395A2: r4=0x0AD258, fr4=fr15=*0xFFFF6354 (ect_gated_c), table_lookup_1D, result stored to 0xFFFF7BC0.
0x039564-0x039594: fr14=1-*0xFFFF7800; float_safe_div(1,fr14) then +(-1) gives x/(1-x), saved at @r15.
0x0395A4-0x0395CC: if byte 0xFFFF7448 == 1, clamp(r, 0, *0xCC3EC); else clamp(r * *0xFFFF7BC0, 0, *0xCC3F0); stored at 0xFFFF7BC0-20 = 0xFFFF7BAC.
0x0395E8-0x03960A: compare with 0xFFFF798C, then copy 0xFFFF7BAC to 0xFFFF7BA8/0xFFFF7BA4 or zero 0xFFFF7BA8.
0x0391D2-0x0391D6: r4=0xAD208, fr4=@r15=rpm_current, lookup to stack+120; 0x039216-0x039224: passed as fr5 to bsr 0x03949E with r4=GBR+32 byte and r5=*0xCBBFF; result to 0xFFFF7BA0-36.
0x038ED6-0x038EE0: whole computation skipped if rpm_current >= *0xCC3C4.
0x036D4C-0x036DCE: float at 0xFFFF7A1C-4 decremented via float_max(x - step, floor) with steps from 0xCC254/0xCC250 and floor 0 or *0xCC24C.
0x0243C6/0x0243C8: GBR=0xFFFF683C; subsequent mov.w/mov.b r0,@(disp,gbr) store quantized ECT, IAT, load, MAF, rpm, 0xFFFF7BA8 (GBR+42) and others.
0x02459C-0x0245AA: fr6=-20.0 (0x024718), fr5=0.3515625 (0x02471C) for axis_frac_to_uint8 of 0xFFFF7E90, stored to GBR+60.
mem-feedback_dont_attribute_from_magnitu.not_shown:
- Clamp limits *0xCC3EC, *0xCC3F0 and *0xCC3C4, the deadband constants, and the step and threshold constants 0xCC24C-0xCC258 / 0xCBC6A-0xCBC6E.
- Body of 0x03949E and of the 0x03961C alternate path.
- Physical meaning of 0xFFFF7800 (the fraction x), 0xFFFF798C, 0xFFFF7E90 and 0xFFFF7A18.
- Who consumes 0xFFFF7BA8/0xFFFF7BA4/0xFFFF7B7C and the 0xFFFF683C block.
- Whether these routines are scheduled or active in this calibration.

doc-architecture-06.mechanism:
This is a patched rev limiter. The stock fuel-cut routine at 0x03B66C compares rpm_current (fr15) against Rev Limit On/Off pairs. Both arms of its float_deadband_check branch (on the 0xFFFF65FC value, window 0..1) were rewritten to jump to injected code at 0x0F1000. The jump target comes from literal-pool words 0x03B79C and 0x03B7A8, which both hold 0x000F1000.

The patch works as follows:
- It loads fr9 = RAM 0xFFFF65FC and the threshold at 0x0F104C (bytes 0x4100D311, about 8.05).
- It reads the byte flag at 0xFFFF65D0 and picks an offset. If the flag is 1: 2700.0 (0x0F1050) when fr9 < 8.05, otherwise 0.0 (0x0F1054). If the flag is not 1: 0.0 (0x0F1048) when fr9 > 8.05, otherwise 2700.0.
- It adds the offset to the rpm register (fadd fr8,fr15).
- It sets r2 = 0x0CC500 (Rev Limit On) and jumps back to 0x03B6B2. The delay slot loads fr8 = Rev Limit On (6700).
- At 0x03B6B2 the stock code loads fr6 = Rev Limit Off (0x0CC504) and runs the normal hysteresis. Cut flag 0xFFFF7CB9 is set to 1 when the adjusted rpm reaches Rev Limit On, and cleared to 0 when it falls below Rev Limit Off.

The net effect is an effective limit of 6700 - 2700 = 4000 rpm while the 0xFFFF65FC quantity is below about 8.05, and stock limits otherwise. That is a launch-style or low-speed rev limiter, if 0xFFFF65FC is vehicle speed (unverified). The offset rpm also feeds the later Rev Limit On(3)/Off(3) comparisons.

Inputs: rpm_current, 0xFFFF65FC, flag 0xFFFF65D0, and the 0x0CC500/0x0CC504 calibrations. Output: bytes at 0xFFFF7CB8+1, +2 and +0, the final cut state. Byte +0 is released only when 0xFFFF620C drops below Rev Limit Fuel Resume (Boost).

Separately, 0x0BB404 clamps RAM 0xFFFF7C78 to at least 8000.0 (from 0x0F8900) with float_max. It uses the result as the threshold in an rpm > threshold test and stores it to 0xFFFF5E28. 0x09A3C2 and 0x09A473 sit in an SSM-style 0xA8 read-memory-by-address handler (reply 0xE8), not in the limiter.

addresses.role: Re-entry point after the patch: loads r2 = 0x0CC504 (Rev Limit Off) and branches to the stock hysteresis compare at 0x03B6C0. The patch jumps here from 0x0F1034. Originally it was the delay-slot or alternate load in the stock code.
Literal-pool word holding 0x000F1000, the hook target used at 0x03B6AE (deadband check true path).
Literal-pool word holding 0x000F1000, the hook target used at 0x03B6B8 (deadband check false path, originally the Rev Limit On(2)/Off(2) branch).

Entry of injected code in erased flash (0xFFFF padding around it). Computes a conditional rpm offset of 0 or 2700 from 0xFFFF65FC versus about 8.05 and flag 0xFFFF65D0, adds it to fr15, forces Rev Limit On (0x0CC500) and returns to 0x03B6B2.
Last byte of the float constant at 0x0F1054 (0.0). This is the rpm offset when flag 0xFFFF65D0 == 1 and 0xFFFF65FC >= 8.05, so no offset is applied.
Rev Limit On (6700 rpm). After the patch it is the fuel-cut-on threshold for both deadband branches, compared against rpm + offset (0 or 2700).

Rev Limit Off (2) (6680). It belonged to the alternate pair selected by the deadband check. That path is now hijacked: the patch overrides r2 and always returns to the 0x0CC504 load, so this value is bypassed.

Float 8000.0, the floor applied with float_max to RAM 0xFFFF7C78 in 0x0BB404. The result is the threshold that fr12 (rpm_current in one mode, or 0x0C4DBC) must exceed, and it is stored to 0xFFFF5E28. Lying outside the normal calibration area, it is probably another patch constant that keeps this rpm threshold at or above 8000.
Holds 0xFFFF with no direct references, possibly an unused or erased cell. Its purpose is not shown.

Instruction (extu.w r4,r5) near the start of a diagnostic read-memory handler. The handler is called with command 0xA8 and builds the 0xE8 reply. 3-byte addresses prefixed 0xFF/0xF2/0xF4 read 1/2/4 bytes; other addresses below 0x350 dispatch through a function table at 0x6423C.
Odd address inside the instruction at 0x09A472 (add #1,r13, the loop counter of the same SSM 0xA8 read handler). It is not a data reference; why it was flagged is not shown.

doc-architecture-06.inert_or_gated:
- The rpm offset is 2700.0 (0x4528C000 at 0x0F1050) only when 0xFFFF65FC is below about 8.05 (0x4100D311 at 0x0F104C). Otherwise it is 0.0 (0x0F1048 and 0x0F1054).
- Flag 0xFFFF65D0 changes the outcome only at exact equality with the threshold, so it is effectively inert.
- Rev Limit On (2)/Off (2) (0x0CC508 = ?, 0x0CC50C = 6680) are bypassed: both deadband arms now jump to the patch, which forces 0x0CC500/0x0CC504.
- In 0x0BB404 the threshold from 0xFFFF7C78 is clamped to at least 8000.0 by 0x0F8900. With an rpm input this makes that comparison unlikely to trip below 8000 rpm.
evidence: 03B6AE: mov.l @(0x03B79C),r0 ;=0x0F1000 / jmp @r0, with delay slot 03B6B2 loading r2=0x0CC504 (Rev Limit Off).
03B6B8: mov.l @(0x03B7A8),r0 ;=0x0F1000 / jmp @r0, with delay slot loading r2=0x0CC508. The patch then overwrites r2.
0F1000-0F102A: fr9=@0xFFFF65FC, fr6=@0x0F104C (0x4100D311 ~8.05), byte @0xFFFF65D0 ==1 selects compare direction, then mova picks 0x0F1048 (0.0), 0x0F1050 (0x4528C000 = 2700.0) or 0x0F1054 (0.0).
0F102E: fadd fr8,fr15, where fr15 = rpm_current loaded at 03B678.
0F1030-0F1036: r2=0x0CC500, jmp 0x03B6B2, delay slot fmov.s @r2,fr8 gives fr8 = Rev Limit On = 6700.
03B6C0-03B6D4: if !(fr8 > fr15), set byte 0xFFFF7CB9 = 1; else if !(fr6 > fr15), clear it.
03B6D6-03B6F2: the same hysteresis against Rev Limit On(3)/Off(3) (0x0CC510/0x0CC514) writes 0xFFFF7CBA, also using the offset fr15.
03B716-03B736: the selected byte (+2 or +1) sets 0xFFFF7CB8=1; it clears when 0xFFFF620C < Rev Limit Fuel Resume (Boost).
0BB452-0BB45C: float_max(fr4=@0xFFFF7C78, fr5=@0x0F8900=8000.0) goes to fr15; then fcmp/gt fr15,fr12 and fr15 is stored to 0xFFFF5E28.
09A400/09A47E: r4=0xA8 (SSM read-memory command); 09A48C writes 0xE8 reply; 09A446: or 0x000F0000 onto the address and copies 1/4/2 bytes for prefixes 0xFF/0xF4/0xF2.
doc-architecture-06.not_shown:
- Physical identity of 0xFFFF65FC (vehicle speed is a hunch; the 0..1 deadband check and ~8 threshold fit km/h) and of flag 0xFFFF65D0 (could be clutch or a state flag).
- What the selector functions 0x22CF4, 0x299AC and 0x299BC return, and the meaning of 0xFFFF5E95.
- The values of Rev Limit Off (0x0CC504), Rev Limit On(2), Rev Limit On(3)/Off(3) and Fuel Resume (Boost).
- What 0xFFFF7C78 holds, and who consumes 0xFFFF5E28 and the GBR flags in 0x0BB404.
- Why 0x0DAE8C, 0x09A3C2 and 0x09A473 were flagged. No direct code links them to the limiter patch. Indexed or GBR-relative accesses to any of these addresses would not appear in this pack.

mem-project_cruise_noncruise_mechanism.mechanism: This is a periodic monitoring/diagnostic scheduler (dispatched from 0x060568, which stages ECT/IAT/RPM/MAF into a scratch frame at 0xFFFF9120 then calls a series of sub-checks via bsr). The sub-function at 0x060ED2 selects one of several RPM-indexed 1D threshold tables (0xAF630/0xAF644/0xAF658/0xAF66C/0xAF680/0xAF694/0xAF6A8) by a mode byte read via a helper at 0x22F92, looks each up against current RPM (passed with index -56 = rpm slot) using table_lookup_1D, and compares the looked-up thresholds against mass_airflow_gps (loaded into fr14 from 0xFFFF85E4) and other scratch values to set GBR-relative result flags (bytes at gbr+99..102, gbr base 0xFFFF90B2). Tables 0xD9BE4 (desc 0xAF630) and 0xD9C44 (desc 0xAF644) are the RPM-vs-airflow limit curves for two of these modes. The sub-function at 0x0610E6 compares a 16-bit measured value at 0xFFFF90B2 against calibration limits 0xD9AD8 (250) and 0xD9ADA (375) plus a float threshold, setting a pass/fail byte at 0xFFFF90C4. The counter routine at 0x061120 increments a 16-bit saturating counter at gbr(0xFFFF90B4)+0 via uint16_add_sat when a condition/edge holds. doc-rev-limit-patch-05.mechanism: This is the engine rev-limiter (fuel-cut) hysteresis logic. Function 0x03B66C compares current RPM (0xFFFF6624 rpm_current, loaded into fr15) against a set of ON/OFF thresholds and maintains a 3-byte fuel-cut flag block at 0xFFFF7CB8[0..2]. The routine first selects which ON/OFF pair to use based on a deadband/condition check (float_deadband_check on the byte at 0xFFFF5E95 vs 1.0/0.0): when the condition is false it branches via the trampoline at 0x0F1000, which applies an RPM offset (fadd of a selected correction into fr15, offset chosen by comparing 0xFFFF65FC against a constant gated by the flag byte at 0xFFFF65D0) and then jumps back into the ON-table arm at 0x03B6B2, loading 'Rev Limit On'(0x0CC500). The two arms load the OFF threshold ('Rev Limit Off' 0x0CC504) or ON threshold ('Rev Limit On (2)' 0x0CC508) into fr6. Standard hysteresis follows: if RPM > ON threshold, set the active-limit byte to 1 (cut); if RPM > OFF/below it, clear to 0 (resume). A second identical hysteresis block at 0x03B6D6/0x03B6E6 uses 'Rev Limit On (3)'(0x0CC510) and 'Rev Limit Off (3)'(0x0CC514) and writes byte @(2,0xFFFF7CB8). Later code combines the flag with a boost-based resume ('Rev Limit Fuel Resume (Boost)' 0x0CC518 vs fr12) and writes the final per-cylinder-or-mode cut byte @0xFFFF7CB8. Function 0x016102 reads 'Rev Limit Off'(0x0CC504) again for a separate low-side comparison. Function 0x03AA00/0x03AAA4 and 0x03D2FE aggregate 0xFFFF7CB8[0..2] along with a large array of other fuel-cut/fault flag bytes into summary/status words.

'Rev Limit On (2)' float32 threshold (6700). Loaded into fr6 at 0x03B6BE as the ON threshold on the branch taken when the deadband condition is true.
'Rev Limit Off (2)' float32 (6680). No direct literal reference in this pack; presumably reached by index or unused in this calibration path shown.
'Rev Limit On (3)' float32 threshold (6700). Loaded into fr8 at 0x03B6D8; if rpm>threshold, second cut flag byte @(2,r5) set to 1.
'Rev Limit Off (3)' float32 threshold (6680). Loaded into fr8 at 0x03B6E8; resume side of the second hysteresis, clears byte @(2,r5) to 0.

Byte[1] is the primary hysteresis state (written 0x03B6CA/0x03B6D4). Byte[2] is the (3)-pair hysteresis state (written 0x03B6E4/0x03B6F2). Read by status aggregators at 0x03AAAC and 0x03D322.

Byte[2] of the flag block: (3)-pair hysteresis state. Written/read via @(2,r5); unreferenced directly because indexed off base.

Code trampoline (not calibration data despite the label). Applies an RPM correction offset to fr15 then jumps into the ON-table arm at 0x03B6B2. Selects one of three offset constants (@0x0F1048, 0x0F1050, 0x0F1054) by comparing 0xFFFF65FC to 0xFFFF65D0-gated constant.

ON-arm entry point in the rev-limiter: loads 'Rev Limit Off' into fr6 (the hysteresis then compares both). Jump target of the 0x0F1000 trampoline.
Entry of the second (3)-pair hysteresis block; loads 'Rev Limit On (3)' and performs the RPM comparison writing flag byte[2].

mem-project_ffb_transient_clamp.mechanism: Two related transient-fuelling paths feed one additive fuel-correction sum. (1) Function 0x038E6E (GBR=0xFFFF7B7C, r10=0xFFFF7BA0) builds a bounded transient correction. It only runs when rpm (0xFFFF6624) is below the constant at 0xCC3C4, the enable byte 0xFFFF90BD is non-zero, and the case 0xFFFF7C68==1 with 0xFFFF7D2E==0 is excluded. Otherwise it branches to 0x039284 and calls a reset/clear routine at 0x0392C4. It first forms a scaling factor: (1+(0xFFFF73E8-1)*k[0xCC3E0]) * (1+(0xFFFF7400-1)*k[0xCC3E4]), stored at 0xFFFF7B98. It reads four state values at 0xFFFF7B7C, 7B80, 7B84 and 7B88. Byte counters at GBR+32..34 (0xFFFF7B9C..7B9E) are incremented with saturation. Flag bits in the bytes at GBR+35 (0xFFFF7B9F) and GBR+36 (0xFFFF7BA0) can force states to zero and reseed them from rpm-indexed tables 0xAC710, 0xAC724, 0xAC738 and 0xAC74C. Gains come from load-indexed tables (0xAD168, 0xAD190, 0xAD17C, 0xAD1A4) and ECT-indexed tables (0xAD1B8, 0xAD1E0, 0xAD1CC, 0xAD1F4). Term A = s1*La*Ea + (fr15*Lc*Ec)*[0xFFFF7B98], clamped by float_clamp_range to [table 0xAD118(ECT), table 0xAD12C(ECT)] and written to 0xFFFF7B90. Term B = s2*Lb*Eb + (fr14*Ld*Ed)*[0xFFFF7B98], clamped to [0xAD140(ECT), 0xAD154(ECT)] and written to 0xFFFF7B94. Their sum goes to 0xFFFF7B8C. The four states are then updated by helper 0x03949E using rpm tables 0xAD208..0xAD244, the counters, and byte constants 0xCBBFF..0xCBC02. (2) Function 0x02FFE4 adds 0xFFFF7B8C, along with 0xFFFF73B4, 7A08, 7A14, 7AF4 and +1, into a total fuel multiplier. The sum also takes in terms 0xFFFF798C, 0xFFFF7A20, 0xFFFF7BA8, 0xFFFF7BCC and minus 0xFFFF7A44. Which combination is used depends on byte 0xCBBD2==90 (max(798C,7BA8) path versus min/max path). The total is multiplied by 0xFFFF7340, offset per cylinder, clamped to [0, 32.0] and written to 0xFFFF730C..0xFFFF731C. (3) The separate throttle tip-in enrichment path (0x03A68C/0x03A9B8) works as follows. Throttle tip-in enrichment A or B is looked up on the throttle-change input 0xFFFF62E4 (A if 0xFFFF844F==1) and stored at 0xFFFF7C54; ECT compensation B/C goes to 0xFFFF7C58. 0x03A68C multiplies the base by: RPM compensation (axis rpm), boost-error compensation (axis 0xFFFF7C50), ECT compensation, optionally Compensation D (0xFFFF7C38, only when throttle input >= 0xCC4A8), and Compensation A (0xFFFF7C44, or 1.0 when 0x23E48 returns 0). The result goes to 0xFFFF7C30. It is applied (0xFFFF7C3C, and 0xFFFF7C40 = value + 0xFFFF734C) only if the throttle input is >= 0xCC4A0 and the result is >= 0xCC4A4. Further conditions: applied-counter < threshold, the throttle-cumulative check, and flags 0xFFFF6254, 0xFFFF726C and 0xFFFF7D18 all zero.

Throttle Tip-in Enrichment A, looked up on 0xFFFF62E4 when 0xFFFF844F==1 and stored to 0xFFFF7C54 as the tip-in base value.
Throttle Tip-in Enrichment B, the alternative used when 0xFFFF844F!=1; stored to 0xFFFF7C54.
Tip-in Enrichment Compensation (RPM), indexed by rpm_current; multiplier on the tip-in base in 0x03A68C.

Additive fuel-correction term. In 0x02FFE4 it is either max'ed with 0xFFFF798C (when 0xCBBD2==90) or added directly into the sum. In 0x03162C it must be below 0xCBE78 as one condition for setting flags 0xFFFF7450 bytes 2 and 3. Its physical meaning is unknown.

Fuel-correction fraction. In 0x02FFE4 it is summed in, with 0xFFFF7A44 subtracted. In 0x0A92BA it forms 1/(1+73A4+798C+7A20), stored to 0xFFFFAF9C+52 and converted to uint16. In 0x03162C and 0x08447C it must lie inside a deadband around 0, together with 0xFFFF798C, to allow a condition and a counter. Identity unknown; it may be a transient/tip-in enrichment fraction (hunch).
Not shown in pack
Entry of a task called from the periodic scheduler 0x047C40 (jsr at 0x047F68), in the same run of fuel tasks as 0x038E30/0x0399EE. Its body is not shown.
Scheduler call site loading 0x036BF4 and jsr'ing to it.
Code inside 0x036C4E-0x036E60; not shown.

mem-project_ffb_transient_clamp.inert_or_gated: Term B upper limit table 0xAD154 is all 0, so term B (0xFFFF7B94) is clamped to [-0.1, 0] and its positive (enrichment) side is inert. Term A is clamped to ±0.1 (written as ±0.099976) at every ECT. Throttle Tip-in Enrichment A and B are identical (424..1568), so the 0xFFFF844F selector has no effect on the base value. The ECT compensation B vs C tables chosen by the same flag are not shown. RPM compensation saturates at 1.9922 from 4800 rpm up. Boost-error compensation reaches 1.0 at 347.8. The 0x038E6E path is gated by rpm < constant 0xCC3C4 (value not shown), enable byte 0xFFFF90BD != 0, and not (0xFFFF7C68==1 && 0xFFFF7D2E==0). Tip-in is gated by thresholds 0xCC4A0, 0xCC4A4 and 0xCC4A8 (values not shown), flags 6254, 726C and 7D18, and the counter limits. In 0x02FFE4 the final multiplier is clamped to [0, 32.0].
evidence: 0x038ED0: r10=0xFFFF7BA0. 0x0391CC-0x0391D0 add the values at r10-16 and r10-12 and store the result at r10-20 = 0xFFFF7B8C.
0x039180-0x03918E: float_clamp_range with min/max taken from lookups of 0xAD118/0xAD12C (stack 104/108) -> 0xFFFF7B90. 0x0391B4-0x0391C2: min/max from 0xAD140/0xAD154 (stack 112/116) -> 0xFFFF7B94.
0x0390B2-0x039156: descriptors 0xAD118, 0xAD12C, 0xAD140 and 0xAD154 are each looked up with fr12 = ect_current.
0x038ED6-0x038EF8: rpm compared with 0xCC3C4, then the 7C68/7D2E check, then the r12 (0xFFFF90BD) check; any failure branches to 0x039284 (bsr 0x0392C4).

0x02FFF8/0x03004E: 0xFFFF7B8C is loaded into fr8 and added into fr14 with 73B4, 7A08, 7A14, 7AF4 and +1. The result is multiplied by 0xFFFF7340, clamped [0, 0x42000000=32.0], and stored at 0xFFFF7340-52..-36.

The contents of the load/ECT/rpm gain tables (0xAD168..0xAD1F4, 0xAD208..0xAD244, 0xAC710..0xAC74C), the threshold constants (0xCC3C4, 0xCC3E0, 0xCC3E4, 0xCC4A0/A4/A8) and the internals of 0x03949E and 0x0392C4 are not given. Writers of 0xFFFF7BA8, 0xFFFF7BCC and 0xFFFF7A20 are not shown. Whether tip-in output 0xFFFF7C3C/7C40 feeds 0xFFFF7A20 is not shown. 0xFFFF683C, 0x036BF4's body and 0x036D14 are not shown. doc-ssm-read-patch-02.mechanism: 0x0006423C is the base of a jump table of 32-bit function pointers (one per entry, indexed by entry<<2). The code at 0x09A45E/0x05F72A/0x09A694 loads this base, shifts an identifier left by 2 (shll2), indexes mov.l @(r0,r5),r6 to fetch a handler pointer, and calls it via jsr @r6. Each table slot holds a ROM code address (pool at 0x06423E onward shows values like 0x0005DEB2, 0x0005DFBA, 0x0005D1D0, 0x0005DCAE, etc., where 0x0005D1D0 recurs as a shared default/stub handler). The function at 0x09A3BA parses a byte-stream record: it reads 3-byte big-endian records (mov.b @r12+ three times into r1, with a type byte in r0 checked against -1/-12/-14), and for a non-special record whose assembled value r1 is below 0x0350 (mov.w @(0x09A4DA)=0x0350 bound check, cmp/hs r8,r1 -> skip if >=), it dispatches through the 0x6423C table using that value as index, storing each handler's byte return into an output buffer at 0xFFFFB3F4. 0x09A4DA holds the constant 0x0350 = table/ID upper bound (the same 0x0350 appears at 0x09A734). 0x09A4E4 is the literal-pool slot holding the table base pointer 0x0006423C used by this function. This is a diagnostic/service (OBD/DID) request handler building a response: it reads a definition list, validates IDs against the 0x0350 limit, calls per-ID getter functions via the dispatch table, and packages a response (calls to 0x0009CFEE/0x0009B770/0x0009CABE and the error path 0x00098686 with negative-ACK codes).

addresses.role: Base of a 32-bit function-pointer dispatch table; indexed by id<<2, fetched pointer called via jsr. Entries point into 0x0005Dxxx handler code, with 0x0005D1D0 as a recurring default/stub.
16-bit constant 0x0350 = upper bound/count for the ID range; used as cmp/hs guard before table dispatch and loop limit.
Literal-pool slot holding the table base 0x0006423C, loaded into r5 before the shll2/indexed fetch and call.

doc-ssm-read-patch-02.inert_or_gated: IDs with r1 >= 0x0350 are gated out (cmp/hs r8,r1 then bt skips dispatch). Table slots equal to 0x0005D1D0 act as a shared default handler rather than a unique one. In 0x09A62A a separate guard rejects slot value 0x0005E76A (cmp/eq r5,r6 -> bt out) before dispatch.
evidence: 0x09A45E: mov.l @(0x09A4E4),r5 loads 0x0006423C; then mov r1,r0; shll2 r0; mov.l @(r0,r5),r6; jsr @r6 -> indexed function-pointer call
0x05F72A/0x05F734: same base 0x0006423C, shll2 of a word at 0xFFFF8F28, mov.l @(r0,r5),r6; jsr @r6
0x09A694/0x09A698: same base, index from @(36,r15) (id<<2), mov.l @(r0,r5),r6; jsr @r6
0x09A414: mov.w @(0x09A4DA),r8 = 0x0350; 0x09A45A cmp/hs r8,r1; 0x09A45C bt skips dispatch when id>=0x0350
Literal pool at 0x06423E+ decodes as repeated 0x0005Dxxx pointers (e.g. 0x0005DEB2, 0x0005D1D0 recurring), consistent with a pointer table
Record parser at 0x09A41E-0x09A444 reads 3 bytes per entry and branches on type bytes -1,-12,-14 (0xFF,0xF4,0xF2)
doc-ssm-read-patch-02.not_shown: The pack does not show the number of entries in the 0x6423C table (0x0350 is the ID bound, not necessarily the table length), the meaning/service of each individual handler (0x0005DEB2 etc.), what the handlers return, the format/source of the parsed record stream, or what RAM 0xFFFFB2F4/0xFFFFB3F4/0xFFFF8F28 semantically represent beyond buffers/ID holders.

doc-architecture-05.mechanism: 0x0BE588 (fmac_interp_uint8) and 0x0BE598 (fmac_interp_uint16) are shared table-lookup/interpolation helper routines, not data despite being tagged 'calibration data'. They are called via jsr with a FPU-register calling convention: an integer index/axis value is loaded (extu.b or extu.w) into r4, fr4 and fr5 are preloaded with float constants from local literal pools (via mova/fmov.s, e.g. fldi0/fldi1 or pool floats like 0x3E99C04A, 0x4080), the helper returns its result in fr0, and the caller stores fr0 to a RAM scratch/output location (fmov.s fr0,@(disp,base)). The uint8 variant is passed byte axis values; the uint16 variant is passed a 16-bit value assembled from two consecutive bytes (low = @(n,gbr), high = @(n+1,gbr) shifted left 8, extu.w). The large functions at 0x0167F4, 0x017ABC and 0x017F20 are structured handlers that: gate on a mode/enable byte (0xFFFF5E40, compared to 1), call uint8_unpack (0x000BE980) / uint8_pack (0x000BE9A0) to read/validate and re-pack status words into gbr-relative slots, walk blocks via helper 0x00005EA4 (with 0x00063690 as a base/record pointer and 0x0000317C / 0x00003190 as acquire/release-style bracket calls), run many bytes through the fmac_interp helpers to convert raw counts to engineering values, and run per-item counters through uint8_add_sat (0x000BE53C) with saturation/threshold checks (constants 63 and -6/0xFA) that set pack flags. 0x002B8C is a routine repeatedly invoked through a dispatch/trampoline table (jsr @r0 then jmp to the next handler) at 0x002080-0x0020C8.

doc-transient-fuel-03.mechanism: 0x03BB6C is the real entry of a periodic speed-limit fuel-cut state machine. The pack's 0x03BB6E bound is one instruction late; 0x03BB6C pushes r14. The task list at 0x049E74 calls it once per pass. Inputs: fr12=[0xFFFF65FC] (inferred vehicle speed, because it is compared with the DEFINITION speed-limit thresholds), rpm=[0xFFFF6624] kept at @r15, fr13=[0xFFFF620C] (unknown signal), and four byte results from helpers 0x1CF16(@4), 0x22CF4(@8), 0x297A0(@12) and 0x299BC(@16). Threshold pair selection: if @8==1 the code uses enable=0x0CC520 and disable=0x0CC528; otherwise it uses 0x0CC51C and 0x0CC524. 0xFFFF7CE0 is the cut-active byte. Bytes +1..+5 of that block are cut output flags, +6 is an inactive-time counter and +7 is an active-time counter, both incremented with uint8_add_sat. Activation (state 0) needs a trigger, rpm >= 0x0CC530 (10000) and @4==0. The trigger is speed >= enable threshold, or @12==2, or @16==2. On activation the flag is set to 1. If the inactive counter is <= 0x0CBC0C, flags +1..+5 are set to 1 and the active counter is preloaded with the 0x0CBC0B value; the inactive counter is then cleared. While active, flags +1, +2 and +5 are set at once and +3/+4 are added once the active counter exceeds 0x0CBC0B. Deactivation happens if @4==1. It also happens when speed < disable threshold, @12==0, fr13 < 0x0CC52C (1260) and @16==0 all hold. It also happens when rpm < 10000 and fr13 < 1260. Then the flag goes to 0. If the active counter is <= 0x0CBC0B, flags +1..+5 are cleared and the inactive counter is preloaded from 0x0CBC0C. While inactive, +3/+4 clear at once and +5 stays 1; all of +1..+5 clear once the inactive counter exceeds 0x0CBC0C. The result is a staged cut entry and release with hysteresis. Small accessors follow the function. 0x03BCD4 returns (0xFFFF7CE0==1), 0x03BCDE returns (0xFFFF7CE5==1), and 0x03BCCC writes 0xFF to 0xFFFF7CE6.

The 0x0F10xx block and 0x0CC500 are calibration constants/tables (rev limit, launch-control RPM/speed thresholds, FFS/LC deltas) in the same calibration region, several unreferenced by direct literals and likely reached via indexed/base access.

doc-knock-07.mechanism: These two floats are threshold constants for a boost-control disable supervisor that watches two engine-health signals: a fine-correction (fuel trim / knock fine correction) value and the IAM (Ignition Advance Multiplier). Function 0x013936 reads a byte at 0xFFFF5D01, converts it to a float (via the 0x00046ACC helper) into fr0, loads the 'Boost Control Disable (Fine Correction)' threshold -2.0 from 0x0C0BF8 into fr8, and tests fcmp/gt fr0,fr8 (i.e. -2.0 > correction, meaning correction is more negative than -2.0). If so it increments a saturating 8-bit delay counter at 0xFFFF5D02 (byte @(1,0xFFFF5D01)) via uint8_add_sat. Function 0x013960 compares that counter against the calibrated delay byte at 0x0C0BAD ('Boost Control Disable Delay (Fine Correction)'); when the counter reaches/exceeds the delay it sets a disable flag at @(4,0xFFFF5D01)=1 and clears the counters, otherwise keeps incrementing. The block at 0x0139B0 handles the IAM path: it loads a float IAM/health value from 0xFFFF3234 into fr8 and the 'Boost Control Disable (IAM)' threshold 0.5 from 0x0C0BFC into fr9, tests fcmp/gt fr8,fr9 (IAM-value > 0.5), and combined with a second threshold at 0x0C0C00, drives a tri-state boost-disable decision stored at bytes under 0xFFFF5D05. So 0x0C0BF8 and 0x0C0BFC are the fine-correction and IAM thresholds that decide whether boost control is disabled.

doc-transient-fuel-02.mechanism: These are the subroutine entry points of a periodic scheduler-driven feature pipeline. The top-level dispatcher at 0x049CF0 (gated by a byte flag at 0xFFFF8EDC) runs a long table of jsr calls; two of them are 0x037186 (the orchestrator) and 0x03BB6C (a neighbour in the same batch). 0x037186 is the feature's main step routine: it loads two config floats (0xFFFF7D68/0xFFFF7D6C) into fr15/fr14, calls a helper at 0x000278DE and stores its byte result to 0xFFFF7A5C, snapshots a sensor float from 0xFFFF69F4 and ect_current (0xFFFF6350) into a local frame based at 0xFFFF7A6C, then calls in sequence the sub-steps 0x037492, 0x03735A, 0x03740C, 0x037450, 0x03726A and 0x0371E6, and finally lag-filters a result into the frame. The listings for 0x03735A and 0x03740C are the same function split by the heuristic (0x03735A is a lag-filter wrapper that falls through into a literal pool; 0x03740C is the next function). The whole mechanism reads engine sensors (coolant temp, mass airflow at 0xFFFF63C4, a float at 0xFFFF63FC/0xFFFF63C4) and a set of enable/mode bytes, computes thresholds and comparisons, and maintains filtered state in the RAM block around 0xFFFF7A50-0xFFFF7A74.
